subject: LumenForge renewal & capacity review
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Jade Lin <jade@lumenforge.ai>, Markus Engel <markus@lumenforge.ai>
Cc: procurement@lumenforge.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: LumenForge renewal & capacity review

Hi Jade / Markus —

Quick summary from our side ahead of the renewal: we ran a usage pass on your account for Q1 and noticed a persistent uptick in generative requests (mainly chat + assistant pipelines) starting mid-February. Attached is a CSV with token-level breakdown by route and peak latency percentiles (lumenforge-usage-q1-2028.csv). High-level:

- Baseline monthly tokens: ~1.8B
- Peak week (Mar Wk3): ~420M tokens (traffic concentrated around real-time assistant endpoints)
- P50 latency: 110ms, P95: 430ms on current plan

We often see this pattern when customers ramp models and then add inference-heavy features; it creates tension between latency SLAs and unit cost. A few questions so we can prepare options:

1) Do you expect this traffic profile to persist or is there a planned pilot concluding in May?
2) Is your procurement/finance team open to a short bridge (3–6 months) rather than a straight annual commit?
3) Any hard constraints on per-token price or discount bands we should avoid?

If you’re available next week I can carve out 30 minutes to walk through the CSV and a couple of pricing scenarios (burst credits, short-term commit, and a 2x capacity uplift).

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[karthik@redwood.com] | +1 415-555-0183
[attachment: lumenforge-usage-q1-2028.csv]

From: Jade Lin <jade@lumenforge.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Engel <markus@lumenforge.ai>, procurement@lumenforge.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Apr 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: LumenForge renewal & capacity review

Thanks Karthik — appreciate the quick analysis and the CSV.

Short answers: the ramp is real and should persist through Q3. We’ve been expanding the assistant into two new product flows which multiply token usage per session. Procurement is looped in on this thread (procurement@lumenforge.ai).

Two asks from our side before a meeting:

- Can you model a 2x baseline commit (with a 20% discount band) and an alternative short-term bridge where we keep current baseline but get burst credits for black swan weeks? We need to show this to finance.
- Do you have concrete ROI examples (customer X who moved to a 6-month bridge then scaled) — numbers that show token-per-dollar improvements after batching/quantization recommendations?

We’re fairly timeline-sensitive — procurement would like a draft SOW/amendment they can review by next Friday.

Best,
Jade Lin
Head of AI | LumenForge
[jade@lumenforge.ai]
[attachment: procurement_rfp.pdf]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Jade Lin <jade@lumenforge.ai>, Markus Engel <markus@lumenforge.ai>, procurement@lumenforge.ai
Date: Fri, 6 Apr 2028 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: LumenForge renewal & capacity review

Monica / Soojin — looping you both in. Jade confirmed the ramp and wants two concrete options (2x commit vs short-term bridge + burst). Procurement needs a draft amendment by next Friday.

Monica — can you draft an operational runbook (expected latency at 2x, burst handling, autoscale limits, rollback path) and include the minimum observability we’ll expose in Console for their SREs?

Soojin — can you run pricing scenarios and a simple ROI sim:
- Scenario A: 12-month 2x baseline commit, 15% discount + 3 months of burst credits (6k credits/mo)
- Scenario B: 6-month bridge at current baseline + on-demand burst credits (prepaid block) + 10% discount

I attached an internal ROI simulation we can use as a starting point (roi-simulation-v2.pdf) and a proposed amendment template (proposed-amendment-2028-04-09.docx).

Goal: reconvene with Jade/Markus early next week for a 30-min alignment and hand them the amendment draft by Friday.

Thanks —
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[karthik@redwood.com]
[attachments: roi-simulation-v2.pdf, proposed-amendment-2028-04-09.docx]

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Jade Lin <jade@lumenforge.ai>, Markus Engel <markus@lumenforge.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, procurement@lumenforge.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: LumenForge renewal & capacity review — recommended amendment & next steps

Hi all —

Thanks for the context, Jade. I put together an operational + commercial recommendation based on the ROI sim and their traffic patterns:

Summary recommendation (attached): proposed-amendment-2028-04-09.docx

- Term: 6-month bridge (May–Oct 2028) with option to convert to a 12-month 2x baseline on mutual agreement
- Capacity: 2x baseline token commitment applied to billing cadence during bridge window
- Burst: 6k burst credits per month (auto-applied during peaks), additional burst billed at on-demand rate
- Discount: 15% off list pricing during bridge in exchange for the commit
- SLA & ops: P95 latency target preserved at current SLA levels; we’ll add a Console dashboard share and an SRE playbook describing autoscale and fallback policies
- Next steps:
  1) Jade/procurement to review the amendment; we can accept redlines on the SOW items (security and data handling) within 48 hours after receipt.
  2) If agreed, DocuSign link below can be used to execute the amendment; we’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff to enable their SREs on Console.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/real-link/example-LF-amendment

Attachments: lumenforge-usage-q1-2028.csv, roi-simulation-v2.pdf, proposed-amendment-2028-04-09.docx

I’ll be available Wednesday morning for the review call — Karthik, please propose 9:00–11:00 PT slots.

—
Monica Patel
